messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — High request rate detected for /v1/batch (P95 latency spike, 5xx increased). paging @channel. link: https://monitoring/reports/incident/1796551234
alex: Acked. I'm oncall. Starting triage. Can someone pull the top client IPs and UA strings?
sara: grabbing logs now. I'm seeing large volumetric bursts from multiple /16s, mostly us-east and eu-west. UA looks botty: "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; curl/7.2.3) scrapers/1.0" and repeated short sessions. token per request low but request count huge. No auth token pattern — looks like anonymous scraping.
tilly: Kibana query I ran:
```
index: requests-* | top client.ip by count | filter path:/v1/batch | group by user_agent
```
Top IP ranges: 45.77.0.0/16, 185.230.0.0/16; repeated GETs every ~0.5s.
mike: probable scraper farm. Recommend immediate mitigations:
1) temporary WAF rule to block UA pattern + those /16s
2) apply dynamic rate limit: 10r/s per IP on /v1/batch
3) consider disabling anonymous /batch for 10m as fallback
Anyone object?
emily: I'll run WAF + rate limit now. Preparing rule:
```
-- WAF rule
rule_id: temp-block-scrapers-1796551234
match: user_agent contains "scrapers/" OR client.ip in [45.77.0.0/16,185.230.0.0/16]
action: block
expires: 10m
```
Applying to edge in us-east and eu-west.
ops-bot: ACTION LOG: WAF rule temp-block-scrapers-1796551234 applied to us-east,eu-west at 1796551320; rate-limit /v1/batch => 10r/s per src ip applied at 1796551380; CDN throttle configured (10kps global burst).
sara: initial effect: request rate dropped ~68% in targeted regions, 5xx back to baseline. Good win. :tada:
alex: nice. Any customer impact?
emily: One large customer (acme-corp) on Dedicated saw elevated 429s for batch calls for ~3m while rate limit in place. They were within quota but many parallel jobs hit the limit. CS notified and paused their background jobs.
cs-team: on it — reached out to Acme, they accepted temporary workaround and asked for credits. Logged ticket CS-4891.
mike: we'll revert the blocking of the whole /16s next if traffic stays low; keep the UA match for another 30m and keep per-IP rate limit until midnight UTC. Also add a canary to avoid collateral damage.
tilly: pulled a few sample payloads — looks like non-JSON or tiny payloads (scrape attempts). Saving samples to /alerts/samples/1796551234.tar.gz for later forensics.
alex: handing off to next oncall @mike in 30m. Create incident in tracker and assign postmortem owner. Actions: (a) identify attacker infra + ASN, (b) tune adaptive bot detection, (c) revisit default quotas for anonymous/batch endpoints, (d) improve alerting to show client tier impact.
incident-bot: Oncall handover: next_oncall=mike, handover_time=1796553034
incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-1796551234
alex: marking this thread resolved for immediate mitigation. Will keep monitoring and will run postmortem after 72h. Thanks team. :heart:
ops-bot: NOTE: rollback plan: remove block for IP ranges -> 1796554800 if no further spike; WAF rule will auto-expire at 1796551934.
cs-team: filing follow-up with Acme for credits and root-cause summary.
